Vercel Pro is a $20 monthly platform fee, not simply $20 per user. Vercel's own documentation describes it that way, and it includes one deploying seat and $20 of monthly usage credit ($20/month Pro platform fee, 1 deploying team seat included, $20/month in usage credit). Each additional deploying seat costs $20 per month, while viewer seats are free (Additional deploying Owner or Member seats are $20 each per month; Viewer seats are free.).

Usage beyond the included allocations is billed on top of that. Pro includes 1 TB of Fast Data Transfer and 10,000,000 Edge Requests per month, and overage is charged against the credit before switching to on-demand billing (Each month, you have 1 TB Fast Data Transfer and 10,000,000 Edge Requests included. Once you exceed these included allocations, Vercel will charge usage against your monthly credit before switching to on-demand billing.).

Some third-party pages still list Pro as $20 per user per month. That matches the older model, and the official docs say legacy Pro teams are being moved to the new pricing model. The official docs are the more reliable source for current pricing. Verify on vercel.com/pricing before budgeting.

Vercel's Pro plan costs **$20 per month** as a platform fee, not simply $20 per user. This comes from a search summary of Vercel's docs. I couldn't open vercel.com/pricing directly because the fetch was refused.

- **Included:** one deploying seat and $20 of monthly usage credit.
- **Extra seats:** additional deploying Owner or Member seats are $20 each per month. Viewer seats are free.
- **Included usage:** 1 TB of Fast Data Transfer and 10,000,000 Edge Requests per month. Overage is charged against your credit first, then billed on demand.
- **Older pricing:** some third-party pages still list Pro as $20 per user per month. That is the older model, and the docs say legacy Pro teams are being moved to the new one.

Check vercel.com/pricing before you budget, since I couldn't confirm it there.
